mainTopic: Which acts and which intentions can make a קרבן פיגול, including pouring the leftover blood and dipping the finger in an inner חטאת.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a question about intentions made while collecting the blood. Planning to collect the blood tomorrow is not פיגול, but planning to pour the leftover blood tomorrow is. A ברייתא then shows that the altar's 'eating' counts for פיגול too. The answer is that it depends on which act the כהן is doing at the time: sprinkling the blood counts, but pouring the leftovers does not. Next, רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא and רבי יהושע בן לוי report that dipping the finger in the blood of an inner חטאת can make it פיגול. רב פדא and ריש לקיש object that פיגול is learned only from שלמים, which have no finger-dipping. After a long back-and-forth, the גמרא arrives at a general principle: whatever makes a קרבן פסול blocks פיגול, and whatever is required for it can create פיגול. רב מרי tries to prove this from a משנה about the מנחה, but the proof is pushed away. Finally, two ברייתות that disagree about dipping are explained as following the רבנן and רבי שמעון, and the גמרא begins to question that answer on the next amud.

steps.title: Two different intentions about collecting the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction between two sources. Slaughtering with intent to collect the blood tomorrow is not פיגול. Collecting the blood with intent to pour the leftovers tomorrow is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no contradiction. One source is about someone who says: 'I am slaughtering in order to collect its blood tomorrow.' The other is about someone who says: 'I am collecting its blood in order to pour the leftovers tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between רבא and the ברייתא by showing they are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting the blood is not a kind of 'eating', so planning to collect it tomorrow does not create פיגול. Pouring the leftover blood on the altar counts as the altar 'eating' it. So collecting the blood with a plan to pour it tomorrow does create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made invalid by an intention to eat or offer it after its proper time
Collecting the blood of the animal in a vessel
In order to / with the intention that
The leftover blood, poured on the base of the altar
Tomorrow, meaning after the allowed time

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases mention 'collecting', but in different roles. In the first case, collecting is what he plans to do tomorrow. In the second case, collecting is the act he is doing right now.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult;
this one is where he says: 'I am hereby slaughtering'
'in order to collect its blood tomorrow,'
that one is where he says: 'I am hereby collecting its blood'
'in order to pour the leftovers tomorrow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to argue about whether an intention during קבלה makes פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: It depends on what the intention is about. Collecting tomorrow is not פיגול. Pouring the leftovers tomorrow is פיגול.

steps.title: A Sage questions רבא about pouring and burning
steps.stepSummary: One of the חכמים asks רבא whether an intention about pouring the leftover blood and burning the אימורים really fails to make a קרבן invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to רבא: Does an intention about pouring the leftover blood and burning the fats not make the offering invalid?!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar challenges רבא. Here he states his question, and the next step gives the source behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar thinks רבא's approach implies that intentions about pouring the leftovers or burning the אימורים do not create פיגול. He finds that surprising, and he will bring a ברייתא to show why.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the Sages (an unnamed scholar)
Pouring out the leftover blood
Burning the fats and parts that go on the altar
Makes invalid

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
And the pouring of the leftovers and the burning of the sacrificial portions –
does intention about them not disqualify?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבא's approach seems to imply about pouring and burning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that intentions about שפיכת שירים and הקטרת אימורים do not make פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Intentions about the altar's 'eating' should count just like intentions about people eating the meat.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts the altar's 'eating' too
steps.stepSummary: The scholar brings a ברייתא. The double word הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל teaches two kinds of eating: people eating and the altar 'eating'. So intentions about pouring the leftovers and burning the אימורים also make פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: You might think an intention works only for eating the meat. From where do we include pouring the leftovers and burning the fats? The verse says 'And if it is at all eaten.' The verse is speaking of two kinds of eating: one is eating by a person, and one is eating by the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar backs up his challenge with a ברייתא that proves an intention about the altar's 'eating' does count for פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק doubles the verb for eating (הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל). From this the ברייתא learns two kinds of eating: by people and by the altar. Pouring the leftover blood and burning the אימורים are the altar's 'eating', so intentions about them should create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
From where do we learn to include
'It is surely eaten': a doubled verb that teaches two kinds of eating
The altar's 'eating': burning or pouring things on it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that the altar's 'eating' counts for פיגול, just like a person's eating does.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא מַחְשָׁבָה מוֹעֶלֶת
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: One might think intention is not effective
except regarding eating the meat;
from where do we include pouring the leftovers
and burning the sacrificial portions?
The verse states: 'And if it is at all eaten' –
the verse speaks of two kinds of eating:
one is eating by a person,
and one is eating by the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that powers the challenge in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That intentions about pouring the leftovers and burning the אימורים do make פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the doubled verb in ויקרא 7:18.

steps.title: It depends on which act he is doing
steps.stepSummary: Answer: sprinkling the blood with intent to pour the leftovers tomorrow makes פיגול. Pouring the leftovers with intent to burn the אימורים tomorrow does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he says: 'I am sprinkling in order to pour the leftovers tomorrow.' That case is where he says: 'I am pouring the leftovers in order to burn the fats tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the scholar. Both kinds of intention can count, but only when they are formed during the right act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling the blood (זריקה) is essential for the כפרה. An intention made during זריקה about pouring the leftovers tomorrow therefore makes פיגול. Pouring the leftovers is not essential for the כפרה, so an intention made during the pouring, even about burning the אימורים tomorrow, does not make פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkles the blood on the altar (זריקה)
Pours out (the leftover blood)
To burn on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: An intention about the altar's 'eating' counts for פיגול. But it only works when it is made during an essential act like זריקה, not during a non-essential act like pouring the leftovers.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not being rejected. Intentions about the altar's 'eating' do count. The point here is which act you must be doing when you form that intention.

phrases.english: It is not difficult; this one is where he says:
'I am hereby sprinkling in order'
'to pour the leftovers tomorrow,'
that one is where he says: 'I am hereby pouring the leftovers'
'in order to burn the sacrificial portions tomorrow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the scholar's challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by which act is being done (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that intentions about the altar's 'eating' never make פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do make פיגול when formed during זריקה, but not when formed during the non-essential pouring of the leftovers.

steps.title: Dipping the finger can make an inner חטאת into פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא says he heard that dipping the finger in the blood of a חטאת פנימית, done with a wrong-time intention, makes the קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה son of רבי חייא said: I heard that dipping the finger makes an inner sin offering פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. A rabbi reports a teaching that one more step of the עבודה, dipping the finger into the blood, can create פיגול in an inner חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the steps that create פיגול were the main jobs: שחיטה, collecting, carrying and sprinkling the blood. Here a new step is added: dipping the finger. For a חטאת פנימית the blood is sprinkled with the finger, so the כהן cannot sprinkle without dipping first. Later steps explain why this might count; step 18 treats it as part of הולכה, carrying the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Dipping the finger into the blood in order to sprinkle it
Makes the קרבן פיגול through a wrong intention about time
An inner חטאת, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל
I heard. He is passing on a teaching he received

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiyya, said:
I heard that dipping the finger
phrases.notes: He means dipping the finger while thinking of eating or burning the קרבן tomorrow.

phrases.english: makes פיגול in an inner sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא: שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The earlier steps asked which intentions make פיגול; this one asks which acts can create it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dipping the finger in the blood of a חטאת פנימית with a wrong-time intention makes it פיגול.

steps.title: רב פדא objects: פיגול is learned only from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: אילפא repeats the teaching to רב פדא, who objects. פיגול is learned from שלמים, and with שלמים dipping the finger does not make פיגול, so it should not make פיגול with a חטאת either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא heard this and said it before רב פדא. He said: Did we learn פיגול from anything other than שלמים? Just as with שלמים dipping the finger does not make פיגול, so too with a חטאת dipping the finger does not make פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פדא challenges רבי יהודה's teaching. He uses the fact that the source of פיגול is the פסוק about שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of פיגול come from the פסוק about שלמים. A שלמים has no finger-dipping step, because its blood is thrown from the bowl. So רב פדא argues that a step which does not exist in שלמים cannot create פיגול in any קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings. The source of the laws of פיגול
Did we learn anything except... It sets up an argument from the source

phrases.english: Ilfa heard it,
and said it before Rav Padda.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כְּלוּם לָמַדְנוּ פִּיגּוּל – אֶלָּא מִשְּׁלָמִים;
phrases.english: He said: Did we learn פיגול from anything except שלמים?
phrases.notes: The פסוק about פיגול, ויקרא 7:18, is written about שלמים.

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים – אֵין טְבִילַת אֶצְבַּע מְפַגֶּלֶת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: Just as with שלמים, dipping the finger does not make them פיגול,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַטָּאת – אֵין טְבִילַת אֶצְבַּע מְפַגֶּלֶת (בהן) [בָּהּ].
phrases.english: so too with a חטאת, dipping the finger does not make it פיגול.
phrases.notes: Some versions say בהן, 'them'; the corrected wording in square brackets is בָּהּ, 'it', since a חטאת is one thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teaching of רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that dipping the finger makes a חטאת פנימית פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All of פיגול is learned from שלמים. שלמים has no finger-dipping step that creates פיגול, so no other קרבן can have one either.

steps.title: Not every rule of פיגול comes from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב פדא. If everything were learned from שלמים, a חטאת brought שלא לשמה should still be able to become פיגול, just like a שלמים. But the halacha is that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did they learn everything from שלמים? If so, just as a שלמים offered not for its own sake is not taken out of פיגול, so too a חטאת offered not for its own sake should not be taken out of פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פדא's starting point, that every detail of פיגול must match שלמים. It shows a case where the halacha for a חטאת is different from שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים brought שלא לשמה is still a kosher קרבן, so a wrong-time intention can still make it פיגול. A חטאת brought שלא לשמה is פסול, and the halacha is that it can no longer become פיגול. So in at least one rule a חטאת does not follow שלמים, and רב פדא's 'everything from שלמים' argument breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it all...? An opening that challenges a sweeping assumption
Offered with the thought that it is a different kind of קרבן
Takes the קרבן out of the possibility of becoming פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'a חטאת שלא לשמה is not taken out of פיגול' is NOT the halacha. It is the strange result the גמרא says would follow if everything came from שלמים. The real halacha is that a חטאת שלא לשמה cannot become פיגול.

phrases.english: But did they learn everything from שלמים?!
If so, just as שלמים offered not for their own sake
are not taken out of פיגול,
phrases.notes: A שלמים brought שלא לשמה is still kosher, so it can still become פיגול.

phrases.english: so too a חטאת offered not for its own sake
should not be taken out of פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind רב פדא's objection in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The premise that every rule of פיגול must match שלמים exactly.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חטאת שלא לשמה cannot become פיגול, unlike שלמים, so not everything is learned from שלמים.

steps.title: Both rules come from extra words in the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a חטאת שלא לשמה cannot become פיגול must come from an extra teaching in the פסוקים. In the same way, the rule that dipping the finger makes an inner חטאת פיגול comes from an extra teaching in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? That rule comes from an extra teaching in the verses. Here too, it comes from an extra teaching in the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes defending רבי יהודה's teaching. It says that rules for a חטאת which go beyond שלמים can come from a ריבוי, an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רב פדא must admit that the חטאת שלא לשמה rule comes from a ריבוי in the פסוקים and not from שלמים. Once that is true, nothing stops a ריבוי from also teaching that dipping the finger can make an inner חטאת פיגול. So the teaching of רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra word or phrase in a פסוק that adds a law
Rather, what do you have to say? You must admit...
Here too. The same reasoning applies to our case

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול is mainly learned from שלמים, but extra words in the פסוקים can add rules that do not fit שלמים. One such rule: dipping the finger in the blood of a חטאת פנימית can create פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the source of a law (שלמים) does not limit every detail of that law when the פסוקים add more.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
It comes from an extra teaching in the verses.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule that a חטאת שלא לשמה cannot become פיגול.

phrases.english: Here too, it comes from an extra teaching in the verse.
phrases.notes: Here 'it' means the finger-dipping rule from step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר – מֵרִבּוּיָא דִּקְרָאֵי קָאָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the pushback in step 7 to answer רב פדא's objection in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel source: a ריבוי in the פסוק teaches rules for a חטאת beyond what שלמים teaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פדא thought that because פיגול is learned from שלמים, only steps found in שלמים can create פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like the חטאת שלא לשמה rule, the finger-dipping rule comes from a ריבוי, so dipping the finger does make a חטאת פנימית פיגול.

steps.title: A second report that dipping the finger makes פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says he heard in the upper room that dipping the finger with a wrong-time thought makes the קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: In this upper room I heard that dipping the finger makes the offering פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second אמורא who reports the same teaching as before: dipping the finger can make a קרבן פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea that רבי יהודה בריה דרבי חייא reported in step 5, now from a different source. It sets up a new round of the same debate, this time with ריש לקיש as the one who objects.

keyTerms.meaning: Dipping the finger into the blood, done before sprinkling the blood of an inner חטאת
Makes the קרבן פיגול when it is done with a wrong-time intention
Upper room, a place where the Sages gathered to learn

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
In this upper room I heard
that dipping the finger makes it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: בַּעֲלִיָּה זוֹ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel report of the teaching from step 5, and this opens a new round of the debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dipping the finger with a wrong-time intention makes an inner חטאת פיגול.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: פיגול is learned from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש objects: all of פיגול is learned from שלמים, and with שלמים dipping the finger does not make פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש wondered about this: Did they learn פיגול from anything other than שלמים? Just as with שלמים dipping the finger does not make פיגול, so too with a חטאת dipping the finger should not make פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי with the same argument רב פדא made earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of פיגול come from the פסוקים about שלמים. A שלמים has no step of dipping the finger, so there is no source for dipping the finger making פיגול. ריש לקיש says a חטאת should follow the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Wondered at, found it hard to accept
Peace offerings, the base case the laws of פיגול are learned from
Is it at all? It opens a strong rhetorical question

phrases.aramaic: תָּהֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish wondered about it:
Did they learn פיגול from anything but שלמים?

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים – אֵין טְבִילַת אֶצְבַּע מְפַגֶּלֶת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: Just as with שלמים, dipping the finger does not make them פיגול,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַטָּאת – אֵין טְבִילַת אֶצְבַּע מְפַגֶּלֶת (בהן) [בָּהּ]!
phrases.english: so too with a חטאת, dipping the finger should not make it פיגול!
phrases.notes: Some versions say בהן (them) and some say בָּהּ (it). בָּהּ fits better, since it refers to the one חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּהֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כְּלוּם לָמְדוּ פִּיגּוּל אֶלָּא מִשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that dipping the finger makes פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פיגול is learned only from שלמים. Dipping the finger does not make שלמים פיגול, so it should not make a חטאת פיגול either.

steps.title: Not everything can be learned from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if everything came from שלמים, then a חטאת שלא לשמה should be able to become פיגול, like a שלמים. But it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did they learn everything from שלמים?! If so, just as with שלמים, bringing it not for its own sake does not stop it from becoming פיגול, so too with a חטאת, bringing it not for its own sake should not stop it from becoming פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers ריש לקיש the same way it answered רב פדא in step 7. There is a rule about חטאת that cannot have come from שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים brought שלא לשמה is still כשר, so it can still become פיגול. A חטאת שלא לשמה is פסול, so it cannot become פיגול. That difference shows that not every rule of פיגול follows the pattern of שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it really so? It opens a challenge
Not for its own sake, meaning the קרבן was brought with the intention of a different type of קרבן
Takes it out of the reach of פיגול, so it can no longer become פיגול

phrases.english: But did they learn everything from שלמים?!
If so, just as with שלמים,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן אֵין מוֹצִיא מִידֵי פִּיגּוּל,
phrases.english: bringing it not for its own sake does not stop it from becoming פיגול,
so too with a חטאת,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ אֵין מוֹצִיא מִידֵי פִּיגּוּל!
phrases.english: bringing it not for its own sake should not stop it from becoming פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind ריש לקיש's challenge in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that every rule of פיגול must come from שלמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule about a חטאת שלא לשמה has no direct parallel in שלמים.

steps.title: Yes, even that rule comes from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says everything does come from שלמים. חוץ למקומו makes a שלמים פסול and keeps it from becoming פיגול. In the same way, שלא לשמה makes a חטאת פסול and keeps it from becoming פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא said: Yes, everything is learned from שלמים. An intention to eat it outside its proper place makes a שלמים פסול, and bringing it not for its own sake makes a חטאת פסול. So just as an outside-its-place intention, which makes a שלמים פסול, stops it from becoming פיגול, so too bringing it not for its own sake, which makes a חטאת פסול, stops it from becoming פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא defends ריש לקיש's approach. He shows how the חטאת שלא לשמה rule can also come from שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is a matching pair. Each קרבן has its own thing that makes it פסול: for שלמים it is חוץ למקומו, and for חטאת it is שלא לשמה. A קרבן that is already פסול cannot become פיגול, so the חטאת rule fits the שלמים pattern after all. That makes ריש לקיש's challenge strong again, since dipping the finger has no parallel in שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Since
An intention to eat or burn the קרבן outside its proper place
Makes the קרבן פסול

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of bad intention. חוץ לזמנו (a wrong-time intention) is what makes פיגול. חוץ למקומו (a wrong-place intention) makes the קרבן פסול but not פיגול, and that is exactly why it blocks פיגול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Yes, everything is learned from שלמים.
Since an outside-its-place intention makes a שלמים פסול,
and bringing it not for its own sake makes a חטאת פסול,
just as the outside-its-place intention, which makes a שלמים פסול,
stops it from becoming פיגול,
so too bringing it not for its own sake, which makes a חטאת פסול,
stops it from becoming פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אִין, הַכֹּל מִשְּׁלָמִים לָמְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 11 and keeps ריש לקיש's approach standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison by matching category: each קרבן's own disqualifier blocks פיגול.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the חטאת שלא לשמה rule had no source in שלמים, so not everything is learned from שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלא לשמה in a חטאת matches חוץ למקומו in a שלמים, so everything really is learned from שלמים.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the comparison breaks down
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the comparison. חוץ למקומו is stronger because it makes every קרבן פסול, while שלא לשמה makes only a פסח and a חטאת פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה says: This comparison breaks from its own side! What is special about the outside-its-place intention that makes a שלמים פסול? It applies to all offerings. Can you say the same about not for its own sake, which applies only to a פסח and a חטאת?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's comparison and shows it does not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוץ למקומו makes every kind of קרבן פסול, so it is a stronger kind of פסול. That strength might be the reason it blocks פיגול. שלא לשמה makes only a פסח or a חטאת פסול, so we cannot assume it has the same power. That means the חטאת שלא לשמה rule still has no source in שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: It breaks from its own side. The comparison carries its own weakness
Applies
Offerings, meaning all the kinds of animal קרבנות
The Pesach offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא tried to learn the חטאת שלא לשמה rule from שלמים. רבי ירמיה broke the comparison: חוץ למקומו applies to every קרבן, while שלא לשמה applies only to פסח and חטאת. So the claim that everything is learned from שלמים is weak again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says: It breaks from its own side!
phrases.notes: He means the two things being compared are not really alike, so the comparison falls apart by itself.

phrases.english: What is special about the outside-its-place intention that makes a שלמים פסול?
It applies to all offerings.
Can you say the same about not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בְּפֶסַח וְחַטָּאת בִּלְבַד?!
phrases.english: which applies only to a פסח and a חטאת?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between חוץ למקומו in שלמים and שלא לשמה in חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חוץ למקומו applies to all offerings, so it is a stronger kind of פסול. שלא לשמה applies only to פסח and חטאת, so it cannot be assumed to work the same way.

steps.title: The rule from שלמים is a general principle, not a case-by-case match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we learn a general principle from שלמים. Whatever makes a קרבן פסול keeps it from becoming פיגול, and whatever is required for it can make it פיגול. The same principle works for the inner חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? With שלמים, a thing that makes them פסול takes them out of פיגול, and a thing that is required for them brings them into פיגול. Here too, with the חטאת, a thing that makes it פסול takes it out of פיגול, and a thing that is required for it brings it into פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem raised by רבי ירמיה. It says we learn a general rule from שלמים, not a one-to-one comparison of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה showed that חוץ למקומו and שלא לשמה are not truly alike, so a direct comparison fails. The גמרא answers that we only need the principle behind the שלמים: what makes a קרבן פסול blocks פיגול, and what is required makes פיגול. For the inner חטאת, שלא לשמה makes it פסול, so it blocks פיגול. Dipping the finger is required, so it can make פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that makes the קרבן פסול
Something required for the קרבן; without it the קרבן does not work
Takes it out of the reach of פיגול
Brings it into פיגול
Here too; the same applies in this case

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול works by principle: what makes the קרבן פסול blocks פיגול, and what is required can create פיגול. That is why dipping the finger in an inner חטאת can make פיגול, as רבי יהושע בן לוי said.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is still matching חוץ למקומו to שלא לשמה one-to-one. That direct comparison was rejected. Now only the general principle is being carried over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי and answers ריש לקיש. Even though everything is learned from שלמים, a step that is required in a חטאת can make פיגול even if שלמים has no such step.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
A thing that makes them פסול
phrases.notes: "Them" means the שלמים, which all the rules of פיגול come from.

phrases.english: takes them out of פיגול,
a thing that is required for them
brings them into פיגול;
here too, a thing that makes it פסול
takes it out of פיגול,
a thing that is required for it
brings it into פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's rejection in step 13 by changing the comparison into a general principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the learning from שלמים is a general principle, not a case-by-case comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the חטאת had to be matched directly to a specific שלמים case, like חוץ למקומו, and the match failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: We take the principle from שלמים: what makes a קרבן פסול blocks פיגול, and what is required makes פיגול. Applied to the inner חטאת, dipping the finger can make פיגול.

steps.title: רב מרי brings a משנה about the מנחה as support
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says a משנה supports this. It lists four steps of a מנחה that can make it פיגול: taking the קומץ, placing it in a vessel, carrying it, and burning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We also learned this in a משנה. This is the rule: anyone who takes the handful, or places it in a vessel, or carries it, or burns it, can make it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings a משנה as proof that a step with no exact match in שלמים can still make פיגול. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא checks the משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four steps of the מנחה that can make פיגול. If one of them has no matching step in שלמים, that would show that a required step alone can make פיגול. This is exactly what was said about dipping the finger.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this in a משנה; this introduces a supporting source
This is the general rule
One who takes a handful from the מנחה
One who places the handful into a vessel
One who carries it to the מזבח
One who burns it on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא –
phrases.english: רב מרי said: We also learned this in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל הַקּוֹמֵץ, וְנוֹתֵן בִּכְלִי,
phrases.english: This is the rule: anyone who takes the handful, or places it in a vessel,
or carries it, or burns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the principle from step 14 and רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a required step with no exact match in שלמים, like dipping the finger, can make פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מנחות that lists four steps of a מנחה that can make פיגול.

steps.title: Which שלמים step matches placing the handful in a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא matches three steps of the מנחה to steps of שלמים. Taking the handful is like slaughtering, carrying is like carrying, and burning is like throwing the blood. But it asks what placing the handful in a vessel matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that taking the handful is like slaughtering, carrying is like carrying, and burning is like throwing the blood. But placing it in a vessel, what does that match?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks each step in the משנה against the steps of שלמים. Three match easily, but one does not. This question sets up how רב מרי's proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all of פיגול comes from שלמים, each step of the מנחה should line up with a step of שלמים. Taking the handful, carrying it, and burning it line up with slaughtering, carrying, and throwing the blood. Placing the handful in a vessel has no clear match, so the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that; this admits some cases before pointing to a problem
This is the same as; it matches
One who slaughters the animal
One who throws the blood on the מזבח
What is it? What does it match?

phrases.english: It makes sense that taking the handful is like slaughtering;
carrying the handful is like carrying the blood;
burning it is also like throwing the blood;
but placing it in a vessel, what does that match?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the משנה רב מרי brought, to find where the proof comes from.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which step of שלמים matches placing the handful of the מנחה into a vessel.

steps.title: Placing the handful does not seem to match receiving the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that placing the קומץ in a vessel matches receiving the blood (קבלה) in שלמים. It rejects this, because blood falls into the vessel by itself, while the כהן actively places the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say placing the handful in a vessel is like receiving the blood, are they really alike? There, the blood falls in by itself. Here, the כהן takes the handful and puts it in himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer to its question from step 16: maybe placing the קומץ in a vessel matches קבלה. It immediately pushes the idea away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קבלה, the כהן just holds the vessel and the blood flows into it on its own. With the מנחה, the כהן himself lifts the קומץ and places it in the vessel. Because the actions look different, the match seems to fail, so the step has no partner in שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the blood of the animal in a holy vessel
By itself, without anyone doing anything
Takes and throws (puts) it in
Are they really alike?

phrases.english: If you say that it is like receiving the blood,
are they really alike?!
There, it happens by itself,
phrases.notes: "There" is the שלמים, where the blood flows into the vessel on its own.

phrases.english: here, he himself takes it and puts it in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 16 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects matching placing the קומץ in a vessel with קבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קבלה happens passively, while placing the קומץ is an active act by the כהן.

steps.title: A necessary step counts even without a match, so dipping counts as carrying
steps.stepSummary: Placing the קומץ in a vessel must be done, so it counts as an important service even without a partner in שלמים. In the same way, dipping the finger in an inner חטאת must be done, so it counts as part of הולכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the handful cannot be offered without placing it in a vessel, it must be an important service. Here too, since the כהן cannot do without dipping, it must count as carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: Since no partner in שלמים was found, the גמרא concludes that a step can count simply because it is required. It then uses this idea to say that dipping the finger in an inner חטאת can make the קרבן פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that a step does not need to match a שלמים step to count. It is enough that the קרבן cannot be done without it. Dipping the finger is required before sprinkling, so it is treated as part of carrying the blood (הולכה).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible (without it)
By force, it must be that
An important service of the קרבן
Carrying the blood toward the place it is applied

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּי דְּלָא יָהֵיב –
phrases.english: Rather, since it is impossible without placing it,
it must be an important service;
here too,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּי דְּלָא עָבֵיד לַהּ –
phrases.english: since it is impossible without doing it,
it must count as carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּי דְּלָא יָהֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the match with קבלה, it explains the step a different way and applies that reasoning to dipping the finger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New principle: a required step counts as a service even without a partner in שלמים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every step that can make a קרבן פיגול must match a step of שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: A required step counts on its own, so dipping the finger counts as הולכה and can make the קרבן פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this holds, the משנה from step 15 proves that dipping the finger in an inner חטאת can make the קרבן פיגול.

steps.title: Placing in a vessel really does match receiving the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Placing the קומץ in a vessel does match קבלה, because both put the main part of the קרבן into a vessel. It does not matter whether this happens by itself or through the כהן's action.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is like receiving the blood. You pointed out that one happens by itself and in the other he takes and places it. But since both are putting into a vessel, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first idea and says the difference raised in step 17 does not matter. This takes away the proof for dipping the finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the result: the offering ends up inside a holy vessel. How it got there does not matter. So placing the קומץ has a match in שלמים, while dipping the finger has none, and the משנה no longer proves that dipping can make the קרבן פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to the first idea)
Putting into a vessel
This one and that one, both
What difference does it make to me?

steps.confusionAlert: Here הָכָא and הָתָם are switched compared to step 17. Now "here" is the שלמים blood and "there" is the מנחה. The point is the same.
steps.whatToRemember: Placing the קומץ in a vessel matches receiving the blood, since both put the offering into a vessel. So the משנה about the מנחה does not prove anything about dipping the finger.

phrases.english: No, it really is like receiving the blood;
and what you said,
"here it happens by itself,
there he himself takes it and places it":

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מַתַּן כְּלִי הוּא,
phrases.english: since both this and that are putting into a vessel,
what difference is it to me if it happens by itself,
or if he takes it and places it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of step 18 by bringing back the match to קבלה that step 17 had rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the מנחה that dipping the finger can make the קרבן פיגול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Placing the קומץ in a vessel does have a match in שלמים (קבלה), so there is no need for the idea that a required step counts on its own.

steps.title: Two ברייתות seem to disagree about dipping the finger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that whether dipping the finger can make a קרבן פיגול is an argument between תנאים. One ברייתא says dipping makes a חטאת פיגול. Another says it neither makes the קרבן פיגול nor is it made פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is an argument between תנאים? One ברייתא teaches that dipping the finger makes a חטאת פיגול. Another teaches that it does not make פיגול and is not made פיגול. Isn't this an argument between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to disagree about dipping the finger. It suggests that this is a real argument between תנאים. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will check whether that is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא treats dipping as a real service, as in step 18. The second treats it as not a service at all, as in step 19. The גמרא asks whether the two ברייתות simply follow these two opposite views.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is an argument between תנאים?
Dipping the finger into the blood before sprinkling
Makes the קרבן פיגול
Is made פיגול (by a thought during a different service)

phrases.english: Shall we say it is an argument between תנאים?
For one ברייתא teaches:
Dipping the finger makes a חטאת פיגול,
and another ברייתא teaches:
It does not make פיגול, and it is not made פיגול;
phrases.notes: "Not made פיגול" means that a thought during slaughtering about dipping tomorrow also does not make the קרבן פיגול.

phrases.english: What, is it not an argument between תנאים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה failed, the גמרא turns to two ברייתות that seem to argue about the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the question of dipping the finger is an argument between תנאים, as the two opposite ברייתות seem to show.

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow the רבנן and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the two ברייתות argue about dipping itself. One ברייתא follows the רבנן and the other follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. This ברייתא follows the רבנן, and that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the two ברייתות are not really arguing about dipping the finger. It assigns each one to a different side of the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that dipping the finger is part of הולכה, carrying the blood. The רבנן hold that a wrong intention during הולכה makes the קרבן פיגול, so dipping can too. רבי שמעון holds that הולכה does not make פיגול, so dipping does not either.

keyTerms.meaning: No. It rejects the suggestion that was just made.
This one... that one. Used to give each source a different explanation.
The Sages, the majority opinion in the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות are not arguing about whether dipping counts as part of הולכה. Both agree that it does. They argue about whether הולכה itself can make a קרבן פיגול, which is the older מחלוקת in the משנה.

phrases.english: No;
this one follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says dipping makes the קרבן פיגול.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; הָא רַבָּנַן, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 20 that the two ברייתות argue about whether dipping is a separate important service.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only rejects the claim that the ברייתות disagree about dipping itself. It keeps the view that dipping is part of הולכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The disagreement can be explained by the known מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון about הולכה. There is no need to invent a new argument about dipping.

steps.title: Why would רבי שמעון single out dipping the finger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the second ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, why does it mention dipping the finger specifically? The גמרא begins to quote something רבי שמעון said.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי שמעון, why does it speak specifically about dipping the finger? Doesn't he say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. It is setting up a quote from רבי שמעון, which continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about wording. If רבי שמעון's view makes dipping the finger no special case, there is no reason to single it out. The quote that comes next will show why mentioning dipping seems unnecessary for him.

keyTerms.meaning: If.
Why specifically this case? Used to ask why a source mentions one particular example.
Dipping the finger in the blood, done before sprinkling the blood of an inner חטאת.
But doesn't he say...? Introduces a statement that seems to contradict what was just said.

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Shimon,
why does it speak specifically about dipping the finger?
Doesn't he say:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי אִירְיָא טְבִילַת אֶצְבַּע? הָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 21's claim that the second ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 21 that the ברייתא saying dipping does not make the קרבן פיגול follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on another statement of רבי שמעון (quoted next), there would be no reason to single out dipping the finger. So the wording of the ברייתא does not fit his view.
